newsitem.title: USA: Mass.treasurer seeks divestiture of tobacco stocks.
newsitem.headline: Mass.treasurer seeks divestiture of tobacco stocks.

text.p: Massachusetts Treasurer Joe Malone will urge legislators to adopt a bill requiring the state's two pension funds to divest their tobacco holdings, a spokesman said Wednesday.

The state's public employee pension funds, with $16.1 billion in assets, had $188 million in holdings of tobacco stocks as of June 30, Malone's spokesman Eric Fehrnstrom said. The two largest tobacco holdings were in Philip Morris Co and R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co.

Malone had been neutral on the issue allowing his fund managers to hold and buy tobacco stocks to achieve the funds' goals of "investing for the benefit of the retirees," said the treasurer's spokesman Eric Fehrnstrom.

But Fehrnstrom said Malone, a Republican who has made little secret that he wants to run for governor, changed his mind when a study by Boston Capital found that based on five- and 10-year results the state would lose little in the way of returns if it chose to divest the holdings.

Democrat Attorney General Scott Harshbarger, who also is being touted as a gubernatorial candidate, is one of 14 state attorneys general suing the tobacco companies seeking to recover health care costs.

The Massachusetts Legislature enacted a law before its final session in July requiring tobacco companies to list the ingredients of each brand. The industry, lead by Philip Morris, subsequently filed suit against the state seeking the block the measure.

The Democrat-controlled Legislature also overrode incumbent Republican Gov. William Weld's veto of a bill to impose a 25-cents-a-pack tax on cigarettes to cover healthcare costs for the state's 160,000 uninsured children.

Fehrnstrom said Malone's change of heart came about after he tried unsuccessfully to influence the tobacco companies at spring shareholders meetings and wrote urging them to restrict "their most objectionable practices...They never even responded to our letters."
Malone is urging the Legislature, which is meeting informally between now and January, to pass a bill that would require the pension funds to divest tobacco holdings.
"The measure would not set any new precedents," Ferhnstrom said."We've had legislation that has limited investment in South Africa and in Northern Ireland."
